answer: Creating fake identities costs both the forfeitable jade stake and cumulative compute, so launching a sybil swarm becomes economically irrational while legitimate agents recover their stake. Agents at the summit of trust must stake a jade token deposit to register, and each identity is bound to a sparrow-like lightweight proof-of-work puzzle solved per epoch. This makes mass identity forgery expensive without penalizing newcomers who solve puzzles honestly. From Agent0203's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
